title: The specified comparison isomorphism
statement:
Let $u:T_1\to T_2$ be proper, let $j_i:X\hookrightarrow T_i$ be
open immersions with $u j_1=j_2$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring and
let $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, as in
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], with $V=T_1\times_{T_2}X$,
projections $b:V\to T_1$, $p:V\to X$ and section $s:X\to V$.
Then restriction of
extension by zero along the
clopen section identifies $b^{-1}j_{1!}K$ with $s_!K$, and
restriction of the
derived direct image identifies
$j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K$ with $Rp_*b^{-1}j_{1!}K$; consequently the
composite

$$
\theta_{u,K}:j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K
$$

is a specified isomorphism, namely the one used in
[def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-section], $b$ identifies $V$ with an open subscheme of $T_1$, and $s$ is an open immersion with closed image and $ps=\operatorname{id}_X$. Also $bs=j_1$ by the defining pair $(j_1,\operatorname{id}_X)$ in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. The square with top $\operatorname{id}_X$, left $s$, right $j_1$ and bottom $b$ is cartesian: if $t:Z\to X$ and $v:Z\to V$ satisfy $j_1t=bv$, then $bst=bv$ and the open immersion $b$ is a monomorphism, so $v=st$. Indeed, identifying $V$ with its open image, the underlying map into $V$ is determined by its composite with $b$, and its sheaf map is determined by restriction of the same composite to opens of $V$. Thus $(\operatorname{id}_X,s)$ gives the inverse of the first projection $X\times_{T_1}V\to X$. Both vertical arrows are open immersions, so this is an open-immersion square as in [def-cbc-open-immersion-square].

source.place: Proof, first sentence; cartesian square written out

proof.text: Apply [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] to that square, with $g=b$, $j=j_1$, $j'=s$ and $g_U=\operatorname{id}_X$. Its finite commutative coefficient hypothesis is exactly the coefficient convention in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison], and $K$ is bounded below by hypothesis. Under the identity inverse-image identification its canonical map gives $e_{u,K}:b^{-1}j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}s_!K$. This proves the first identification using the specified base-change map, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of these objects.

By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] the sheaf functor $j_{1!}$ is additive and exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms when applied degreewise. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], if $\mathcal H^r(K)=0$ for $r<n$, then $\mathcal H^r(j_{1!}K)\cong j_{1!}\mathcal H^r(K)=0$ for $r<n$. Thus $L=j_{1!}K$ belongs to $D^+(T_{1,\Et},\Lambda)$, as required for the next step.

source.place: Proof, application of derived-open-restriction: bounded-below input

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] with $f=u:T_1\to T_2$, $a=j_2:X\hookrightarrow T_2$ and $L=j_{1!}K$. Its fibre product is exactly $V$, its open projection is $b$, and its restricted morphism is $p$. This gives the restriction isomorphism $r_{u,K}:j_2^{-1}Ru_*j_{1!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*b^{-1}j_{1!}K$. No proper-base-change theorem is being applied here: the cited statement is open restriction for an arbitrary scheme morphism.

The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-clopen-section-direct-image] hold by Step 1: $s$ is open with closed image, $ps=\operatorname{id}_X$, and $K$ has the stated finite coefficients and lower bound. Its component-restriction isomorphism is $c_{p,s,K}:Rp_*s_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$.

The functor $Rp_*$ sends $e_{u,K}$ to an isomorphism: its inverse is $Rp_*(e_{u,K}^{-1})$, since functors preserve identities and composition. Therefore $c_{p,s,K}\circ Rp_*(e_{u,K})\circ r_{u,K}$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $r_{u,K}^{-1}\circ Rp_*(e_{u,K}^{-1})\circ c_{p,s,K}^{-1}$. The three maps used in Steps 2, 4 and 5 are respectively the base-change, open-restriction and component-restriction maps specified in [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Its displayed definition of $\theta_{u,K}$ is exactly this composite, so the isomorphism proved here is the specified one.

def properOpenIdentification (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {T₁ T₂ X : Scheme.{u}} (f : T₁ ⟶ T₂) [IsProper f]
    (j₁ : X ⟶ T₁) (j₂ : X ⟶ T₂) [IsOpenImmersion j₁] [IsOpenImmersion j₂]
    (h : j₁ ≫ f = j₂)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₂).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj
      ((rightDerivedLowerStarPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj
        ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K)) ≅
      K
